question: Constant returns to scale (CRS) is a property of production function that holds when ___________.

options.text: a proportional increase in all inputs results in an increase in output by more than the proportion
a proportional increase in all inputs may results in an increase in output by less than or more than the proportion
a proportional increase in all inputs results in an increase in output by less than the proportion
a proportional increase in all inputs results in an increase in output by the same proportion

solution:
The correct answer is __**a proportional increase in all inputs results in an increase in output by the same proportion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• There are **three types **of returns to scale: increasing returns to scale, constant returns to scale, and decreasing returns to scale.
 
• When all inputs in a production process are tripled, the scale of production is increased by a factor of three.
 
• If the output is also tripled, then there are constant returns to scale, because the increase in output is proportional to the increase in inputs.
 
• However, if the output is more than tripled, then increasing returns to scale apply.
 
• This means that the increase in output is greater than the increase in inputs, indicating that the production process is becoming more efficient as the scale of production increases.
 
• On the other hand, if the output is less than tripled, then decreasing returns to scale apply. This means that the increase in output is less than the increase in inputs, indicating that the production process is becoming less efficient as the scale of production increases.
